_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for RTO lead-assignment rules. Edit here only - three places read
this file and previously carried hand-copied duplicates of these values:
- scripts/lead_priority.py   (the Python cron that actually writes assignments)
- api/_lib/db.js             (awbPrefixRules, for leads recorded via the disposal path)
Kept under api/_lib/ specifically because deploy.yml bundles only api/ into the Lambda:
anywhere else and db.js would throw at runtime unless the packaging step changed too.
Values are DATA only - the tier ordering and the round-robin loop are still implemented
once per language (Python cannot execute JS), but both are driven entirely by what's here,
so tuning reasons/quota/prefixes needs no code change in either.
assignmentQuota was the one value that had already drifted: Python used 20 while the CRM
preview used 10, so the preview predicted assignments for half the real quota.
_highPriorityNote: Tier 1 - COD whose ORIGINAL system/courier RTO reason contains one of these (case-insensitive substring). The consignee has already refused or OTP-verified the cancellation, so the outcome is effectively known and worth acting on quickly. Prepaid is tier 0 and wins outright regardless of reason.
highPriorityCodRtoReasons: consignee opened the package and refused to accept
kyc|customer refused to share kyc/ ndc/ scd
_lowPriorityNote: Tier 3 - deliberately behind even 'every other COD order' (tier 2). These OTP outcomes are handled last in the assignment queue.
_awbPrefixNote: Delivery partner from an AWB code's prefix, first matching prefix wins. Business rule confirmed manually against known AWB ranges - nothing in the AWB format itself is self-describing.
